analysis.title: European Equity Strategy: Is Europe's macro recovery running out of steam?
key_insights: BofA sees Euro area domestic growth rolling over. The composite PMI new orders index rose to 52.4 in September, the highest since early 2023, then fell 1.7 points to 50.7 in October, the first pullback since the recovery began. The base case is a move below 50 in the near term.
Three drivers of the recovery are weakening. Financial conditions have tightened, European gas is above €100/MWh, and US growth is expected to slow from an unsustainable pace.

The ECB Bank Lending Survey showed credit conditions tightening the most in almost three years, with expectations pointing to a sharper tightening next quarter. BofA reads this as consistent with the Euro area credit impulse falling back below zero.
German 10-year yields are up about 75bps since the start of the Iran war. France's 10-year yield is up 170bps since February, the second-sharpest rise in over 20 years after 2022.

BofA stays negative on European equities. The macro projections imply 10% downside for the Stoxx 600 to 580 by Q2 next year and about 5% to 610 by year-end, from a 2% fade off the early-August record high.
The main reason for the cautious equity view is the risk of disappointment in the AI capex cycle. AI model commoditisation and falling token prices could weigh on AI monetisation and spending.
Germany is cut from overweight to marketweight. German equities outperformed the market by about 5% since mid-year and the forecast trajectory implies only marginal further upside.
Mining is raised from underweight to marketweight after 15% underperformance since early September, which leaves only marginal downside to the forecast trajectory.

BofA stays underweight cyclicals versus defensives, consistent with underweights in AI capex beneficiaries (semis, capital goods) and overweights in food & beverages and personal & household goods. Cyclicals have underperformed defensives by over 10% since June.

Overweights include small versus large caps (about 5% upside), telecoms (about 15%), real estate (over 15%), France, Switzerland, UK, utilities, pharma, quality, food & beverages and luxury goods (consumer durables, over 30% upside by early next year).

France is moved to overweight. It has underperformed by over 20% since 2024 on political instability, its 12-month forward P/E is at a 7% discount to Europe (around the largest since 2016), and the projections skew positive.

Underweights include banks (nearly 5% underperformance), insurance (about 10%), financial services (5%+), semis, capital goods, Spain, Italy, value versus growth (about 10%) and software is marketweight.

Marketweight calls: airlines, autos, chemicals (about 15% implied downside), construction materials, energy (nearly 25% implied downside but kept at marketweight on US/Iran tensions), mining, software and Europe versus global equities.

AI capex fragilities: US hyperscaler 12-month forward capex rose from under $300bn in early 2025 to $1tn and is expected to reach $1.25tn by 2028. Hyperscaler ROIC fell from 21% to 15.5%, and CDS spreads and funding costs have risen. Oracle's CDS is above its 2008 level.
Ramp AI data show token volumes rising while total AI spend is little changed since July, because token prices are falling.
The correlation between the MSCI Europe AI Capex Select index and European cyclicals versus defensives has risen above 90%, from 25% a year ago.

BofA expects Stoxx 600 12-month forward P/E to de-rate from 13.9x to 13.5x on a higher equity risk premium. Its macro projections imply 7% downside to forward EPS, with 9% EPS growth in 2026 and 4% in 2027, both below consensus.
Stoxx 600 sensitivities: each 3pt fall in the Euro area PMI lowers fair value by about 5%, and each 100bp rise in the real yield lowers it by about 5%.

Markets price a further 70bps of Fed hikes over the next year on top of the September hike, with the Fed funds rate heading to 4.4% against the Fed's neutral estimate of 3.25%. BofA expects real yields to fall as global growth weakens.
BofA expects US high-yield spreads to widen. CCC and lower spreads are already widening and the MOVE bond volatility index has spiked.
US-Iran: Strait of Hormuz tanker transits are effectively zero again, prediction markets give 9% odds of normalisation by January, the SPR is at its lowest since 1982 and US gasoline is $5.1/gallon.

US growth is strong: final private domestic demand contributed 4.2ppts to Q3 GDP growth, and the US composite PMI new orders was 58.1, an eight-year high ex-Covid. Economists expect core PCE just over 3% for the rest of 2026.
The global composite PMI is at an eight-year high of 54.2, and BofA expects it to decline. China GDP growth is expected to slow to 4% by Q2 next year.

Lower Bund yields imply over 15% outperformance after the recent underperformance.
The correction since mid-September looks overdone and projections imply about 15% outperformance.

Wider credit spreads and lower Bund yields imply nearly 5% further outperformance.
Outperforms when risk premia widen and yields fall. About 2% further upside implied.
Risk that AI capex disappoints. Price relative is up nearly 100% since April last year, with nearly 5% further near-term underperformance implied.
AI air pocket risk, wider high-yield spreads and a falling Euro area PMI. Modest further downside implied.
Expected market and bond yield downside. About 10% downside implied after recent outperformance.
Euro area PMI and bond yield downside. 5%+ renewed underperformance implied.

earnings_insights: Macro projections are consistent with Stoxx 600 EPS growth of 9% in 2026 and 4% in 2027 (BofA estimate), both below bottom-up consensus.
BofA projections imply 7% downside for Stoxx 600 12-month forward EPS from the current all-time high.
Stoxx 600 12-month forward EPS rose 16% since end-February (consensus basis), and EPS momentum reached a four-year high, overshooting its usual link with the global PMI.
Tech is expected to contribute over a quarter of global profits over the next twelve months, an all-time high.

risk_factors: AI capex disappointment from commoditised models, falling token prices and weak monetisation.
Rising French and peripheral bond spreads and tighter financial conditions.
An unsustainably strong US economy that slows and drags on external demand.
Sustained high oil prices from the Strait of Hormuz standoff, which BofA notes has historically been associated with recessions.
A sharp spike in credit spreads, which could offset the benefit of lower yields for real estate.
charts_described: Exhibit 44 shows Strait of Hormuz tanker crossings back at effectively zero after a pick-up following the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding.
Exhibit 28 shows record outperformance of high- versus low-momentum stocks in Europe this year before a sharp pullback since mid-June.
Exhibit 27 shows the correlation between the MSCI Europe AI Capex Select index and European cyclicals versus defensives above 90%, versus 25% a year ago.
Exhibit 19 shows US hyperscaler ROIC falling from 21% last year to 15.5%.

vol_and_positioning: The MOVE US bond volatility index has spiked, typically associated with wider US high-yield spreads.
Cross-sector dispersion in Europe remains close to a level seen only three times since the financial crisis.
The Stoxx 600 equity risk premium is near a 20-year low, and the Euro Stoxx 50 ERP fell below 4% for the first time in over 20 years.
European momentum had record outperformance of high versus low momentum earlier this year, then a sharp pullback since mid-June.
CCC and lower US high-yield spreads are widening while overall spreads stay near lows.
geopolitical: US-Iran war and the Memorandum of Understanding: Strait of Hormuz tanker transits have fallen to effectively zero again after a pick-up following the signing.
Prediction markets give a 9% probability that Strait of Hormuz traffic normalises by the start of January.
Ongoing Middle East supply constraints are keeping European gas storage low heading into winter.
French political instability and next year's Presidential election are adding pressure to French spreads.
The US SPR is at its lowest since 1982.

tension_points.bull_case: The Euro area PMI rebounded to a near four-year high, German fiscal stimulus is coming, and domestic assets still show forecast upside (small caps about 5%, telecoms about 15%, real estate over 15%).
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter credit conditions, gas above €100/MWh and slowing US demand point to a PMI below 50 and about 1ppt below-trend domestic demand growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Euro area PMI that stays above 50 rather than falling below it.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex is $1tn and expected to reach $1.25tn by 2028, and consensus expects a prolonged profit boom with 3-year forward EPS growth at a five-year high.
tension_points.bear_case: Commoditised models and falling token prices cap monetisation. Hyperscaler ROIC has fallen to 15.5% and CDS spreads are rising, which could cut AI spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex ending when expected returns fall below the cost of capital, as in past cycles.
